title: Audit PR 201 KUFO Three-Autumn and KSHIP lineage without importing real-token, stale UI, or weakened compile-baseline changes
reason: PR 201 is a 240-commit-stale real-token candidate with 14 KUFO/KSHIP product paths plus three cross-product 11520 paths. Historical exact-head checks are green, but the KUFO lineage model allows unsolicited lot fragmentation to push an account beyond the 64-lot traversal ceiling and make full-balance movement fail, the branch removes the existing TempleHeart V3.3.2 compiler baseline, it overwrites an existing KSHIP path, and its burn/mint/registry pipeline lacks current deployment, registry, governance, and production authority. The safe action is an evidence-only audit. No candidate path is transplanted and downstream PRs 211 and 212 remain blocked.

inventory.selected_runtime_defect: Unsolicited micro-transfers can create more than 64 active lineage lots for a recipient, after which a full-balance transfer reverts at the traversal ceiling.
inventory.security_blocker: Real KAIOS burn, KUFO/KSHIP mint and mutable Organ Registry resolution remain deployment- and authority-sensitive, while the compile-tool change removes a frozen TempleHeart baseline regression input.

blocking_findings: PR 201 is open, Draft, unmerged, currently non-mergeable, 36 commits ahead and 240 commits behind exact latest main.
The PR contains 14 Product 05 paths plus three 11520 HUD/browser paths. Those UI paths are cross-product scope and are all stale relative to the current main shell or tests.
KUFOV4 permits any holder to transfer tiny fragments to another address, each creating or appending lineage lots. The recipient cannot reject those transfers.

Once an account has more than 64 live lots, a movement that needs traversal beyond 64 reverts with LotTraversalLimit. The exact-head test intentionally proves 65 lots make a full transfer fail, but does not protect against an external sender dusting a victim into that state.

The 64-lot ceiling therefore is not only fail-closed complexity control; without receiver opt-in, consolidation, bounded per-account admission, or an aggregation design, it is an externally triggerable token-liveness denial-of-service surface.

KAIOSAlchemyFurnaceV4 burns real KAIOS and immediately triggers KUFO minting through an Organ Registry-resolved output. Registry controller, delayed mutation, deployment binding, and current KAIOS burn compatibility require protected production evidence.

The KGEN gate observes only current balance. It does not prove durable ownership or prevent borrowed same-transaction balance proof; this may be intentional policy but cannot be promoted to production without explicit Canon and economic-risk approval.

The candidate changes the existing KGEN-KAIOS/contracts/KSHIP.sol path while claiming immutable deployed-history preservation. A versioned successor path and explicit deployed-address lineage are required to avoid source identity ambiguity.
The compile-contracts change removes the git-bound TempleHeart V3.3.2 baseline source from compilation. This weakens an existing regression boundary unrelated to Product 05 and must not be imported.

The candidate workflow uses actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4. Historical green results remain valid for that head, but current main uses newer action generations and broader security suites.
Downstream PR 211 rewrites Product 05 paths and depends on #201; PR 212 depends on #211. Neither child may advance before the parent contract, scope, authority, and liveness defects are resolved.
Repository-owner comments and green CI are engineering evidence, not deployment, registry, signer, governance, token, Life, Worker, or Human authority.
positive_findings: The candidate keeps KGEN as a balance observation and contains no KGEN transfer, burn, lock, allowance, holding-age, or tax-history path.
KAIOS burn, output proof consumption, KUFO proof minting, and KSHIP carrier-proof minting are replay-checked and beneficiary-bound within the candidate design.
Three-Autumn targets preserve birth age across transfers and terminally consume residual dust at the third Autumn.
Historical exact-head KUFO, Game Product QA, and Universal Exchange workflows all succeeded at 8b4ccd8c008886f82853ba0f0c064b9217e73894.
The historical 390x844 screenshots are useful evidence for that old shell, but do not validate the candidate against present main.
safe_successor_requirements: Start from exact latest main on a non-codex branch and limit scope to Product 05 contract, policy, test, and review files.

Prevent unsolicited lot-fragmentation denial of service through receiver consent, deterministic lot aggregation, a safe per-account admission rule, or another design that preserves full-balance transfer liveness under hostile dusting.
Add adversarial EVM tests where third parties repeatedly dust a victim, then prove the victim can still transfer and mature the complete balance within bounded gas.
Use versioned successor contract paths or an explicit immutable deployment-lineage manifest; do not overwrite a path that ambiguously represents prior KSHIP history.
Preserve the TempleHeart V3.3.2 compile baseline and all current compile, workflow-security, native-market, Universal, Game, and Responsive suites.

Bind furnace, output, KUFO, KSHIP converter, and Organ Registry endpoints to exact reviewed deployment configuration with delayed-governance, role, receipt, and address evidence before any chain action.
Treat current-balance-only KGEN proof as an unresolved economic policy unless Human Canon explicitly approves its flash-balance and borrowed-balance consequences.
Keep PRs 211 and 212 Draft and unmerged until a safe exact-current-main Product 05 successor is independently testable; dependency order cannot be bypassed.
Do not deploy, transfer, burn, mint, appoint, sign, dispatch, pay, govern, launch an agent, or mutate chain state as part of this audit.
